Probably needs https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/100618 since the GC.* trick is not reliable to get object size in tests.

Otherwise should be ready. The rules turn out to be a bit complex, e.g.
```cs
[StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential, Size = 1000)]
class ClassA
{
    long A;
}

[StructLayout(LayoutKind.Explicit, Size = 1000)]
class ClassB
{
    [FieldOffset(0)]
    long A;
}
```

Here, CoreCLR allocates 1016 bytes for an instance of `ClassA` and 24 bytes for `ClassB` - I am not sure whether it should be "fixed" in CoreCLR, but I aligned NAOT/R2R, so the rules are:

- Classes:
  - Layout has gc pointers - we ignore explicit Size
  - LayoutKind.Explicit - we ignore explicit Size (bug-to-bug compat?)
- Structs:
  - LayoutKind.Sequential + gc pointers - we ignore explicit Size
  - Layout has gc pointers - we align up size to target pointer

So for classes, the only case when we respect `Size` is `LayoutKind.Sequential` + no gc pointers.

Questionable behavior in CoreCLR (Main) for (boxed) object size:
1) For a class without gc refs, why do we ignore `Size=` for `LayoutKind.Explicit`, but not for `LayoutKind.Sequential`?
2) For a struct with gc ref(s), should we ignore `Size=` for even `LayoutKind.Explicit` ? (we do for `LayoutKind.Sequential`). Since gc references can easily "invalidate" explicit Size by AlignUp(8).

cc @jkotas

> Probably needs https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/100618 since the GC.* trick is not reliable to get object size in tests.

I do not think it would help you. This API gives you the exact same result as `sizeof`.

The layout logic is shared with crossgen2; this also reproes with ReadyToRun.

The type layout has been owned/worked on by the crossgen2 team since it needs to be bug-for-bug compatible with CoreCLR VM type system for ReadyToRun to work. Moving to crossgen2 area path.

review_comments: Should this maybe not have the if and multiply the pointer size appropriately in each case?
I prefer expected value to be a constant rather than computed expression for Asserts
I feel like this should print `1000` on both runtimes instead? I don't think anything documents that oversizing is not supported for classes.

The StructLayout and FieldOffset attributes were designed to control the marshalled unmanaged layout. `LayoutKind.Explicit` is fully respected for the marshalled layout. `Console.WriteLine(Marshal.SizeOf<MyClass>())` prints `1000` for my example as expected.

Later ExplicitLayout got overloaded to control overlapping of fields in the managed layout. This overloading introduced many non-sensical behaviors. User code should not depend on managed layout (except blittable structs) in the first place.
